Aditya,

Attaching GridPay's redlines to the MSA and the related Order Form focused on the SLA and support terms. Legal has flagged three areas they consider non‑negotiable for procurement approval:

- Uptime target: 99.95% as a committed SLA (they've crossed out Redwood's 99.9%).
- Service credits: linear credits up to 30% for multi‑day outages, with no cap per incident.
- Maintenance windows: limit to one 4‑hour monthly window per region; emergency maintenance requires 48h notice except for security patches.

We're trying to keep momentum on procurement calendar — can your legal/ops team review and get back with concessions by Friday?

Elena — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. We're reviewing internally today. Quick notes from product/ops that will shape our position:

- Uptime: 99.95% is above our standard hosted tier for this SKU; we can explore a dedicated SLA for Reserved Capacity, or a tiered approach (99.9% baseline with a 99.95% premium option).
- Credits: unlimited per‑incident caps create financial risk. We can accept a higher cap per quarter or a staircase model tied to uptime bands.
- Maintenance: 4h monthly is tighter than our planned rolling patch windows; we can agree to a bounded monthly window + a separate security patch process with advance notice where feasible.

I'll coordinate legal/ops tradeoffs and share a concrete counterproposal by EOD Monday. Copying Lauren (legal) and Laura (ops) to align.

From: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Subject: FW: MSA & Order Form — SLA redlines (uptime / credits / maintenance)

Team — forwarding GridPay's redlines. High level proposed positions for negotiation below; please flag any legal/ops non‑starters before I send to Elena at ~17:00 UTC.

Key asks from GridPay we need to address: uptime=99.95%, uncapped incident credits, 4h monthly maintenance window limit, 48h notice for emergency maintenance.

Proposed counter (concise):
- Uptime: Offer a two‑tier SLA on the Order Form: 99.9% standard; 99.95% premium at +25% monthly fee and subject to dedicated capacity or region‑specific redundancy. (Rationale: technical and cost delta for consistent 99.95%).
- Service credits: Replace 'uncapped per incident' with a quarterly cap equivalent to 60% of one month’s committed spend and per‑incident maximum equal to 30% of monthly committed spend. Include a staircase credit schedule: 99.9–99.0% = 10% credit, 99.0–95.0% = 25% credit, <95.0% = 45% credit, subject to investigation and force majeure carveouts.
- Maintenance windows: Agree to a maximum of two scheduled windows per month not exceeding 6 hours total, with a guaranteed 7‑day notice for standard maintenance. Security patches: notify within 48 hours of scheduling when actionable; emergency patching allowed with post‑incident report and best‑effort advance notice.

Operational asks for Laura: can you confirm whether the premium 99.95% SLA can be technically supported via our multi‑AZ Reserved pools for GridPay's deployment? If yes, what's the delta in monthly unit cost (ballpark percent)?

Legal (Lauren): please validate the credit caps and force majeure carveouts. Also propose wording for the investigation period (e.g., 30 days to validate incident) and audit rights.

I've attached a draft 'proposed_counter_redlines.pdf' with inline edits. If we can align quickly, I'll send a clean counter to Elena with the DocuSign link.

Thanks — Adi

Elena — thanks for the patience while we reviewed. Attached is our counterproposal (proposed_counter_redlines.pdf) and an SLA response matrix that shows how credits map to measurable availability intervals. High‑level summary of concessions we can make now: 

1) Uptime: We can offer 99.95% as an Order Form option under a Premium Availability addendum. This will require GridPay to be on a Reserved Capacity plan and include an additional monthly fee (we propose +25% of the committed spend). We can document this as a separate SLA bucket on the Order Form so your procurement team can choose it.

2) Service credits: We cannot accept unlimited uncapped credits per incident. Counterproposal: per‑incident cap = 30% of one month’s committed spend; quarterly cap = 60% of one month’s committed spend. Credits will follow a graduated band schedule (see attached SLA_response_matrix.xlsx). Credits are payable only after exhaustively validated incidents and a standard 30‑day investigation window; investigation delays extend the payout schedule.

3) Maintenance: We agree to tighter controls: no more than two scheduled maintenance windows per month, up to a combined 6 hours, with at least 7 days’ notice for standard maintenance. Security/emergency patches are allowed with best‑effort advance notice; in those cases we'll provide a post‑action report within 5 business days.

Next steps: 1) Please review the attached proposed_counter_redlines.pdf and the SLA_response_matrix.xlsx. 2) If GridPay agrees in principle, sign the Order Form addendum via the DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABC123-gridpay-msa. 3) We'll schedule a 30‑minute ops handoff to iron out monitoring/alerts and define the dedicated pool sizing if you select the premium SLA.

Happy to jump on a call if that helps — propose Wed 15 Sep 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC.

Best regards,
Adi (on behalf of Redwood Legal & Ops)
Aditya Rao
